Hi Jonas,

We’re expecting a microburst next week tied to an A/B test ramp — roughly 6–8 hours of 3x baseline traffic. Legal wants clarity on how overrun billing will be handled if we hit the burst. Also need a PO timeline and a simple invoice estimate for finance to sign off.

Marc and I reviewed your public docs but we need a concrete operational playbook (who toggles, what metrics trigger rollback, how credits are applied). Can you send a proposal today?

Caroline — thanks for the clear ask. High level answer: yes, we can provision a gated microburst uplift with a staged true-up (escrow) and predefined rollback triggers. I attached a concise playbook describing the steps. Key points up front:

- Short-term uplift: We can open a temporary quota window for 72 hours (configurable) tied to your project tag.
- Escrow / true-up: Tokens consumed beyond your committed threshold during the window are held under a provisional invoice. If the post-window 7-day average falls below X% of uplift baseline, we prorate and credit back per the agreed formula.
- Rollback triggers: auto-rollback if 15-minute P95 latency > 1s OR sustained drop below 60% of uplifted QPS for 30m. Manual rollback option for Triloop SRE is available.
- PO / billing: we’ll provide an estimate and a DocuSign-ready addendum.

I’m looping in Sean (billing) and Ben (solutions) to confirm pricing bands and PO timing. Draft playbook attached.

Jonas Weber

Caroline / Marc — quick pricing note to simplify signoff. Two options:

1) Metered escrow (recommended for this use): uplift is charged at a premium uplift rate (25% over retail per-token rate) and placed in provisional billing. After the measurement window we apply a post-window reconciliation and any applicable credit to the next invoice. No long-term commitment required.

2) Short-term committed uplift: you pre-purchase an uplift block for the window at a 12% discount vs option 1, committed via PO. We can credit back unused capacity up to 30% of the block.

For quick exec signoff, option 1 is fastest — we provision immediately when we receive a signed email. Option 2 needs PO + procurement lead time.

Also FYI the rollbacks Jonas proposed are standard; we log trigger events and send an automated incident summary to your SRE channel. If you prefer, we can set the rollback sensitivity lower/higher.

Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Billing & Programs, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai
